summary:
The SL-096 code does what the design and the accepted review findings asked. I found no defect in what was written.

Scanner.CountListingOpen (Scanner.cs:332-347):
- It counts a parent out only after a child folder's keep-open succeeded. The check is `!io.KeptLastAccess` returns first, and KeptLastAccess is reset at every Open (SynchronousIoCancel.cs:492).
- It acts only at or under the Windows folder. That folder is held as `\\?\` through LongPath.NormalizeRoot, and null when the environment names none (Scanner.cs:118-122).
- It counts each parent out at most once, through the per-scan OrdinalIgnoreCase set.
- Parents are always counted before their children on the single DFS thread, so the order holds. Kept stays between 0 and asked.

TempTree, the two reorders, the Windows-folder Facts, TempTreeRootTests, the corpus tests and the triage doc all match the design and its declared deviations.

What I ran on this PC (Windows 11 26200, not elevated):
- The acceptance bug project: exit 0, 1/1. The Core DLL was confirmed to contain the correction.
- The full suite as the engine runs it (TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP): 789/789, exit 0.
- The full suite under the user's own TEMP (C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp): 789/789, exit 0.
- LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests with detailed output:
  - kept 4 of 7, 4 still old, moved root/plain/links, for the as-is, lower-case and trailing-separator roots;
  - the refusing child: kept 1 of 2, 1 still old;
  - outside the Windows folder: 7/7/7.
- Fitness check: every declared rule holds.
- RuleCases C-001 AGREE: 18 facts, 22 twinned, 48 patterns, 65 settled.
- RuleCases C-003: its checks printed ok, but the script exited 1 because its cleanup's Remove-Item was denied under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. That is pre-existing tooling, filed below as an extra.

Leftovers: C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests lists 0 entries afterwards, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-tests holds only the 4 folders from before this slice, and no testhost processes are left.

SIDE EFFECT OF THIS REVIEW: my C-003 run probably left one scratch folder, C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\fsa-parity-case-<10 hex>. This user cannot list C:\Windows\Temp, so I could neither confirm it nor remove it. A person with admin rights should remove it, together with the survey's fsa-sl096survey-* leftover.

Every case on the matrix feeds its shape in. Two notes:
- The trailing-separator row cannot reach the branch it once named, because Scan trims the separator first. It is labelled a redundant spelling check, as m5 accepted.
- The set's case-insensitivity can never be exercised: every parent string derives from its child's path, so the spelling always matches. The location test's case-insensitivity is exercised by the lower-case row.

Both deferred rows still hold against the code:
- Fixtures can no longer land in %SystemRoot%\Temp through TempTree().
- The correction sits behind `asked` and KeptLastAccess.

The slice index shows no loop: one build attempt.

The test-tooling leak is the only finding, filed as an extra: RuleCases.ps1 builds its scratch folders under the inherited TEMP and removes them with Remove-Item.

Second round: Second round: I fed inputs to the rules and readers this diff adds, aiming to get past them. One new finding: rule 2 is claimed closed as a class, but it misses everyday spellings of the Windows folder's Temp. I took the 7 patterns from .taad/fitness.yaml the same way SettledPatterns reads them and ran each candidate line through them. These lines all got through:
- the `\\?\` extended form: `@"\\?\C:\Windows\Temp\..."` and `"\\\\?\\C:\\Windows\\Temp"`. This codebase writes paths in that form everywhere (TempTree.ExtendedRoot, LongPath.ToExtended, IsAtOrUnder);
- the folder split across Path.Combine arguments: `Path.Combine(@"C:\", "Windows", "Temp")`;
- `%SystemDrive%\Windows\Temp` expanded;
- the GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows, SpecialFolderOption.X) overload combined with "Temp";
- an interpolated drive root followed by `Windows\Temp`;
- `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariables()["TEMP"]`.

None of these is a row in SystemRootTempRouteCorpus.json. I also measured a widening: three patterns catch all of them. They stay quiet on the corpus's Q05, Q06 and Q08 shapes and fire on no code line in any non-excepted Core.Tests file.

Everything else I tried held:
- **The skip family.** The reflection check pins the exact Fact or Theory type, rejects any foreign attribute and Skip on data rows, and reads the same FsaDefaultTestFilter property that VSTestTestCaseFilter uses. So a namespace-qualified custom attribute on the three existing tests is caught there, even though the line pattern misses it.
- **SettledPatterns.** It reads the first entry with a given name. A second appended copy could only add patterns, never remove them. The pinned pattern counts (7 and 6) catch a truncated read.
- **CountListingOpen.** KeptLastAccess is reset at every Open. The InsideExcludedStore exit comes before counting. A failed listing after a successful open correctly still counts the parent out. Kept cannot go below 0.
- **ChooseTestsRoot.** It checks the inputs before calling NormalizeRoot, which would throw on them.

Nothing else I found is new. The RuleCases scratch leak from round 1 still stands as an extra.

findings.claim: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 makes its scratch folders under [IO.Path]::GetTempPath(), which is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP in the engine's shells, and deletes them with Remove-Item in a `finally`. Remove-Item is denied there (SL-089's lesson, and this slice's survey). Measured in this review: `RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-003` under the engine's TEMP printed its checks ok, then threw 'Access is denied' at line 859 and exited 1 without reaching 'All checks held.'. Its scratch folder (fsa-parity-case-<10 hex>) is left in a folder this user cannot list, so nobody without admin rights can find or remove it. Any stage that runs RuleCases (C-003..C-014) as the engine runs it will report a false failure and leak an unrecoverable folder per temp dir. This tooling is outside SL-096's diff and outside rule 2's Core.Tests scope, but it is the same environment fault this slice triaged.
findings.evidence: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:71 New-TempDir roots at GetTempPath(); :859 the finally cleans up with Remove-Item. Observed: C-003 exit 1 with 'Remove-Item: ... RuleCases.ps1:859 ... Access is denied.' under TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP.
findings.fix: In New-TempDir, root scratch folders the way TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot does: use %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when GetTempPath() is at or under the Windows folder. Delete with [IO.Directory]::Delete($dir, $true) inside a try/catch that records rather than throws.
findings.class_of: test tooling that builds scratch under the inherited TEMP (C:\WINDOWS\TEMP in engine shells)

findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1144-1150, rule 'no Core test builds a fixture in %SystemRoot%\Temp except the deliberate one'. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SystemRootTempRouteCorpus.json has no extended-form, split-Combine, %SystemDrive%, SpecialFolderOption or GetEnvironmentVariables() row. Measured with the yaml patterns compiled as SettledPatterns compiles them.
findings.fix:
Add three patterns to rule 2:
- `(?i)\bWindows(\\{1,2}|/|"\s*[,+]\s*@?")Temp\b`
- `(?i)SpecialFolder\.Windows\b[^;\r\n]*?\)\s*[,+]\s*@?"(\\{1,2})?Temp\b`
- `(?i)GetEnvironmentVariables\s*\(\s*\)\s*\[\s*"(TEMP|TMP|SystemRoot|windir)"`
Measured: these fire on every line above, stay quiet on the corpus's C:\WindowsTemp, C:\Windows.old\Temp and System32\drivers samples, and hit no code line in any non-excepted Core.Tests file.
Add corpus rows (now=fire, before=quiet) for the seven lines above, and raise EachCorpusHoldsRowsTheDeclaredPatternsLetThrough's pinned count from 7 to 10.
findings.class_of: routes into %SystemRoot%\Temp that bypass TempTree's redirect

obligations.evidence: Ran `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-096-LastAccessUnderWindowsTemp/SL-096-LastAccessUnderWindowsTemp.Tests.csproj`: Passed 1, Failed 0, Skipped 0, exit 0. src/FsAnalyser.Core/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows/FsAnalyser.Core.dll (09:42) is newer than Scanner.cs (09:35) and contains `_keptUnderWindows`, so the stale-DLL trap did not apply. The bug test still asserts `LastAccessKept <= unmoved` at line 139.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:65-80 (AChildThatRefusesWriteAttributesLeavesItsParentCountedAsKept) builds R\refusing\x.bin in C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests with a 0x100 deny on `refusing` and asserts kept == folders still old. My run printed 'kept 1 of 2; 1 of 2 folders still at least 47 h old; moved: none'. An attempted-open rule would count R out and give 0 against 1, so the test discriminates. The code keys on io.KeptLastAccess (Scanner.cs:337).

No Windows 10 machine (Q-205), and nothing under %ProgramData%/%ProgramFiles% was measured. Writing there is a person's step. ScanResult.cs:197-205 and the triage doc's Limits section record both as unmeasured and uncorrected. This is honest, but it is not a discharge.

The standing check is the Theory at LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:37-59, which asserts LastAccessKept == folders still old. Only `_lastAccessKept--` (Scanner.cs:345) lowers kept. Without it, kept = asked = 7 while 4 stay old, which the equality rejects; spike 3 measured this 3/3. I reasoned it and did not re-run the mutation.

.taad/fitness.yaml rule 'no Core test builds a fixture in %SystemRoot%\Temp except the deliberate one' bans Path.GetTemp(Path|FileName), CreateTempSubdirectory, the TEMP/TMP/SystemRoot/windir env reads and literal spellings. except_files adds FailCriticalErrorsTests.cs and CloudPlaceholderTests.cs, with a comment at CloudPlaceholderTests.cs:282-285. The corpus test passed in my full runs, and Fitness check reports every rule holds. Grep shows Path.GetTempPath in Core.Tests only in the three excepted files.

Scanner.cs:118-122 WindowsFolderFromEnvironment returns LongPath.NormalizeRoot(GetFolderPath(Windows)).Win32, or null when the path is empty or not fully qualified. It is held once per Run (Scanner.cs:157), and CountListingOpen skips the correction when it is null (:340).

Rule 1 in .taad/fitness.yaml has `\bSkip\w*\s*=`, `\bTrait(Attribute)?\s*\(`, the custom *Fact/*Theory pattern and the FactAttribute/TheoryAttribute subclass pattern. LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.TheWindowsFolderFactsRunInTheDefaultSuite (:82-120) checks by reflection that the class is public, each test has one stock Fact/Theory and no Skip, and the default filter has no by-name clause.

ScanResult.cs:190-207 now words LastAccessKept as the structural rule. It says nothing is read back, and lists the gaps: within the hour or updates off, a -1 set that fails after a successful open, ProgramData/ProgramFiles, the spelling-matched root, and the root's parent.
No scratch-copy procedure remains. The committed Theory is the regression check, and the refusing-child Fact pins the spike-1 direction.
LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:35 labels the trailing-separator row a spelling check only. Scanner.Scan normalises the root first (Scanner.cs:64).
The Theory 'as-is' row builds NestedFolders (root, plain and links each with two child folders) in C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests. My run printed 'kept 4 of 7; 4 of 7 ... moved: <root>, plain, links'.
Ran `eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx` with this shell's TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: Passed 789, Failed 0, exit 0.
Ran the full suite (--no-build) in a child pwsh with TEMP=TMP=C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp; GetTempPath printed that path. Passed 789, Failed 0, exit 0.

InTree (LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:111-117) disposes the tree and asserts the \\?\ root is gone. TempTree.Dispose (TempTree.cs:258-296) restores the deny ACL before Directory.Delete. After my runs, C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests lists 0 entries.

cases.evidence: LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:37-59 'as-is' row: 7-folder/4-file tree (root, plain and links each with two child folders) in C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests, back-dated deepest first (OrderByDescending(Depth)), real Scanner.Scan, asked 7 and kept == still old. Ran: kept 4 of 7, moved root/plain/links.

LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:65-80: R\refusing\x.bin with Deny(refusing, 0x100), x.bin back-dated then R, refusing exempt. Ran: kept 1 of 2, 1 still old. The attempted-open rule would give 0 against 1.

'lower-case' row scans tree.Root.ToLowerInvariant() = c:\windows\temp\fsa-tests\<guid> against GetFolderPath's C:\WINDOWS. Ran: kept 4 of 7. It exercises IsAtOrUnder's case-insensitivity. The set's case-insensitivity cannot be exercised, because parent strings derive from the child's own path.
'trailing-separator' row feeds tree.Root + '\\' to Scan. Ran: kept 4 of 7. As m5 said, Scan trims the separator before the set sees it, so this is only a spelling check. It is labelled so at :35.

OutsideTheWindowsFolderEveryKeptFolderStaysKept (:83-98) uses TempTree() and first asserts the root is outside the Windows folder. Under the engine's TEMP the tree was in C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\fsa-tests: kept 7 of 7, 7 still old.
Ran the full suite with TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP: 789/789, exit 0.
Ran the full suite with TEMP=TMP=C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp: 789/789, exit 0.
TempTreeRootTests.cs:19-27 feeds C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\, c:\windows\temp, C:\Windows\Temp\deeper\ and C:\Windows\ against windowsDir C:\WINDOWS and expects the LocalAppData\Temp\fsa-tests redirect.
TempTreeRootTests.cs:38-45 feeds C:\WindowsTemp\, C:\Windows.old\Temp\ and C:\Windows2\Temp; each stays <temp>\fsa-tests.

TempTreeRootTests.cs:48-59 feeds the systemprofile and ServiceProfiles LocalAppData paths and an empty one. Each asserts InvalidOperationException naming TEMP, the Windows folder, 'system or service profile' and the remedy.
The refusing-child Fact holds a deny FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES ACE inside C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-tests, and InTree asserts the root no longer exists after Dispose. fsa-tests listed 0 entries after my runs.

The Theory's equality assert (AssertKeptIsTheFoldersStillOld) is the standing check. Without the decrement, kept = 7 against 4 still old, measured by spike 3 d1-d3 and the builder's mutation. I did not re-run the mutation.

Deferred by the design, and the reason still holds: HeldOpenTreeTests and LastAccessTests use TempTree(), which now always builds outside the Windows folder, so the reorders (HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:238, LastAccessTests.cs:70) are never fed the luafv location. The Windows-folder Facts cover the effect there.

Deferred by the design, and the reason still holds in code: CountListingOpen returns before any correction when `asked` is false or io.KeptLastAccess is false (Scanner.cs:334-338). An SMB share, a cloud folder, a sync root or the excluded store never reaches it.

drift: TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot (TempTree.cs:54-68) has two branches the design did not name and the build did not declare. An empty or unqualified Windows folder uses TEMP as-is. An empty or unqualified LOCALAPPDATA is refused by name. Both are tested (TempTreeRootTests WithNoWindowsFolderNamedTheTempIsUsedAsItIs and the "" refusal row). They are harmless and consistent with review m1.

The Scanner's class remarks (Scanner.cs:22-26) say a child's kept open moves its parent's last access 'under the Windows folder' in general. Only %SystemRoot%\Temp was measured. ScanResult.LastAccessKept's remarks state that limit precisely, so the class summary is the looser of the two texts.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-096/critique-1.json, critique-review-1.json, design-slice-1.json, index.json: engine records, not code. I read none of them; the brief carried what I needed.
tests/bugs/SL-096-LastAccessUnderWindowsTemp/*: the engine's unchanged acceptance test. I only spot-read its assertions (line 139, `LastAccessKept <= unmoved`) and ran it.
